correctness.rationale: Each host edge is uniquely an arrow u->v. Two selected arrows are compatible exactly when tails are distinct and not used as other arrow heads, giving a unique function from tail set to complement. Inclusion-maximality is proved equivalent to onto, yielding full coefficient formulas and minimal cardinality. At even n, minimum maps are oriented perfect matchings; fixed m-1 arrows force the last underlying pair, giving hypercube components. At odd n, minimum maps form one centered triple and m-1 oriented pairs; all valid replacements are proved to be one pair flip or moving one triple leaf to a pair center, giving degree 3(m-1). Four explicit small reconfiguration paths prove connectivity on five labels, lifted to arbitrary odd order by five-label local moves and generation by transpositions. An independently constructed graph-level checker matches all coefficients and swap components for orders 2 through 9. The finite computation does not prove the infinite result; the displayed proof does.

value.rationale: The objects are natural optimal inclusion-maximal induced matchings, a graph-theoretic obstruction to extending a strong matching. The full cardinality enumerator counts all solutions, while the optimal swap graph measures ability to navigate between locally irredundant optimal solutions. The strong parity transition, from exponentially many isolated hypercube components at even order to a connected regular graph at odd order, is a mathematically motivated structural classification, not a routine scalar substitution or arbitrary low-order slice.
